devotionals.title: A Year Full of Thanks
devotionals.scriptureText: “For the Lord is good and his love endures forever; his faithfulness continues through all generations.” Psalm 100:5
devotionals.body:
As the year comes to a close, Psalm 100 feels like a gentle invitation to pause and back with a thankful heart. This psalm is joyful because it remembers who God has been. And when we look back on our own year, we begin to see the same thing: a trail of quiet mercies, steady provision, and a God who never once stepped away.

1. Gratitude grows when we remember who God is. Joy doesn’t come from a perfect year. It comes from a faithful God. Even in the moments that stretched us, confused us, or humbled us, God remained good. He remained nearby. Gratitude begins when we slow down long enough to see His fingerprints on the days we rushed through.

2. We give thanks because we belong to Him. There’s something deeply comforting about ending the year with this truth: we are His. Not because we performed well. Not because we held everything together. We are His because He made us, loves us, and keeps us. That belonging has carried us through more than we realize.

3. Thanksgiving opens our hearts to worship. Gratitude is how we walk into God’s presence. It’s how we close the year – with open hands, not clenched fists. With remembrance, not regret. With praise, not pressure. Thanksgiving doesn’t erase the hard moments. It reminds us that God was present in every high and every low.

This psalm invites us to end the year with a full heart. To look back and see God’s goodness woven through the days we understood and the days we didn’t. His love didn’t run out. His faithfulness didn’t fade. And as we step into a new year, we do so with confidence in the God who has carried us this far and will carry us still.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for Your goodness this year. Thank You for the moments that lifted me and the moments that shaped me. Please teach me to end this year with gratitude and begin the next with trust.

devotionals.title: I Will Do a New Thing
devotionals.scriptureText: “See, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it?” Isaiah 43:19
devotionals.body:
These words were spoken to a people who felt stuck in exile, stuck in disappointment, stuck between what God had done before and what they couldn’t yet see. They remembered the Red Sea, the miracles, the victories. But their present reality felt nothing like those stories. Into that tension, God speaks with a steady, tender voice: I’m not done. I’m doing something new. In case 2025 was rough and you stepped into this new year with fear and uncertainty, be assured that God will do a new thing in 2026.

Here are three truths from this passage

1. God reminds us of His power so we can trust Him again. God brings up the past not to trap us in it, but to anchor our faith. He’s saying, “You’ve seen Me work before. You’ve watched Me make a way where there was none. Hold on to that.” When we look back, we don’t cling to old seasons. Instead, we cling to the God who carried us through them.

2. God invites us to release what we can’t change. “Forget the former things; do not dwell on the past.” This is God freeing us from living in our old memories. He knows how easily we replay old wounds, old failures, old disappointments. He knows how the past can quietly shape our expectations. So, He gently says, “Let it go. I’m leading you somewhere new.”

3. God is beginning His new work now. The wilderness represents confusion. The wasteland represents exhaustion. And God chooses those exact places to reveal His new work. He doesn’t wait for ideal conditions. He brings life where life shouldn’t exist. He makes paths where there were none. He provides water where everything felt dry.

This passage invites us to lift our eyes in 2026 and believe that God is not limited by what we’ve lost in the previous year(s) or what we fear. He is the Redeemer, the Holy One. And when He says He is doing something new, He means it. Even if we can’t see it yet, it is already beginning to spring up.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank you for bringing me into this new year. Please make a way in my wilderness and let Your living water refresh my soul as I journey into the year

devotionals.title: In Christ
devotionals.scriptureText: 3 Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us... in Christ. Ephesians 1:3
devotionals.body:
Apostle Paul begins Ephesians with two simple words that carry the weight of the entire Christian life: in Christ. Those two words describe the truest thing about our identity, our security, our story, and our future. Before Paul tells us how to live, he tells us where we live: inside the grace, love, and purpose of Jesus.

Here are four truths from today’s passage

1. In Christ, we are chosen. Our life didn’t begin with our mistakes or our achievements. It began with God’s decision to love us. Before time existed, God set His affection on us. Being “in Christ” means our identity is not fragile. It is rooted in eternity.

2. In Christ, we are adopted. God didn’t tolerate us into His family. He welcomed us with joy. Adoption means belonging. It means we are not an outsider trying to earn acceptance. We are sons and daughters, fully received and fully loved.

3. In Christ, we are redeemed. Our past no longer defines us. Christ’s sacrifice has rewritten our story. Redemption means the stains we thought were permanent have been washed away. Forgiveness isn’t a theory; it’s the air you breathe now.

4. In Christ, we are included in God’s eternal plan. God is weaving a story that stretches across heaven and earth, and somehow, we are part of it. Our life is not random. It is connected to God’s purpose, God’s timing, and God’s glory.

This passage invites us to rest, not in your performance, but in your position. We are in Christ, held in His grace, rooted in His love and secure in His purpose. And nothing in heaven or on earth can change that. This is our destiny once we come to know Jesus. It is the position the blood of Jesus bought for us. Do you know Jesus yet?
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You that my life is hidden in Christ. Help me live from the security of Your love, the freedom of Your forgiveness, and the purpose of Your calling.

devotionals.title: Sealed in Christ
devotionals.scriptureText: “…when you believed, you were marked in him with a seal, the promised Holy Spirit…” Ephesians 1:13
devotionals.body:
Apostle Paul continues his explanation of what it means to belong to Christ. These verses are identity statements. They are not abstract theology. They tell us who we are, where we stand, and what God has already secured for us. Paul wants believers to live with a deep, unshakable confidence that our life is not random, our salvation is not fragile, and our future is not uncertain.

Here are three truths from today’s passage

1. In Christ, we are sealed by the Holy Spirit. “When you believed, you were marked in him with a seal…” God places His Spirit in us as His mark, His declaration that we belong to Him. This seal is a mark of ownership, protection, and authenticity. We don’t have to wonder if we are accepted. We don’t have to fear being lost.

2. The Spirit is our guarantee of a future we cannot lose. “…the promised Holy Spirit, who is a deposit guaranteeing our inheritance…” The Spirit within us is the first taste of the fullness to come. He is God’s guarantee of our inheritance in Christ. We have an unshakeable assurance. Our inheritance is not wishful thinking. It is guaranteed by God Himself. We are His possession, and He will finish what He started.

3. We live for the praise of His glory. “…that we… might be for the praise of his glory.”. Paul is reminding us that our hope in Christ becomes a living display of God’s beauty, mercy, and faithfulness. We exist to reflect Him. Our lives are not accidents. They are testimonies of God’s grace shining through us.

This passage invites us to breathe deeply, to rest in the truth that our identity is secure, our salvation is sealed, and our future is guaranteed. We are chosen, included, sealed, and kept, to the praise of His glory. The Holy Spirit Himself is our seal, the guarantee of our inheritance in Christ!
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You that my life is held in Your purpose. Thank You for choosing me, sealing me with Your Spirit, and securing my future in Christ.

devotionals.title: Eyes to See
devotionals.scriptureText: “…that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened in order that you may know the hope to which he has called you…” Ephesians 1:18
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul prays for the people who have received salvation. He isn’t praying for material blessings or easier circumstances. He’s praying for something deeper; that believers would truly see. That they may see the fullness of what it means to belong to Christ.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Spiritual growth begins with revelation, not effort. Paul knows that knowing God isn’t something we achieve. It’s something God reveals. The knowledge of God that births true transformation, comes by revelation. Here, Paul is praying that the Father would open our understanding so we can know Him; not just know about Him, but know Him personally, intimately, deeply.

2. God wants to open the eyes of our hearts. The “eyes of the heart” means the inner place where we perceive truth. It's the place where we understand who God is and who we are. Paul prays for clarity, illumination, and spiritual sight. He knows that when our hearts see clearly, everything else changes.

3. Our calling becomes real when God opens our eyes. Paul wants us to grasp the weight of our calling, the hope that anchors us, the inheritance that awaits us and the glory that surrounds us. These are realities God wants us to experience with spiritual clarity. Unless our eyes are opened, we cannot understand these realities.

This passage invites us to slow down and ask God to help us see. To see His heart. To see His purpose. To see the hope that is already ours in Christ. When the eyes of our heart are opened, our faith deepens, our understanding grows, and our lives begin to reflect the glory of the One who called us.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please open the eyes of my heart. Give me the Spirit of wisdom and revelation so I may know You more deeply.

devotionals.title: The Resurrection Power
devotionals.scriptureText: “…his incomparably great power for us who believe. That power is the same as the mighty strength he exerted when he raised Christ from the dead…” Ephesians 1:19
devotionals.body:
Paul wants believers to understand something incredible: the power at work in us is the same power that raised Jesus from the dead. Not a lesser version. Not a diluted form. The same power. How incredible!

Here are three truths from this passage.

1. The resurrection power is available to us. If you want to know what God can do, look at the empty tomb. He brings life out of death, hope out of despair and victory out of defeat. The resurrection is God’s declaration that nothing, absolutely nothing, is beyond His reach. And Paul says this incomparably great power is “for us who believe”. This power is directed toward us. It is active, personal and present with us, in us and for us.

2. Christ reigns above every power, seen and unseen. Paul lifts our eyes to the throne to see the enormity of God’s power in Christ so we can understand what we have in Him. He is enthroned above every earthly and spiritual power. Every name, every system, every force, present or future, bows beneath Him. This is the Christ who holds us, leads us, and intercedes for us.

3. We are His body, filled with His fullness. This is one of Paul’s most breathtaking statements. The church is not a building or an institution. It is Christ’s body. His life flows through us. His presence fills us. And His fullness shapes us. His authority is exercised for the good of His people. Everything He governs, He governs with the church in mind.

This passage invites us to live with confidence in the risen Christ who reigns above all things and fills His people with resurrection power. We are not powerless. We are not abandoned. We are held by the One who conquered death and rules forever.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please help me live with the confidence that comes from knowing You reign above every power and every name
